interest: Shows pre-WWII suspicion of a Japanese 'commercial mission' as espionage cover, expelled from the Dominican Republic for excessive photography.
overview: Despatch No. 615 (Feb 1939): Hinkle reports the Dominican government expelled a five-member Japanese 'commercial delegation', suspected of espionage for its lack of real business and excessive photography; the group sailed for Havana on the SS Cuba.

people.name: Eugene M. Hinkle
people.role: U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Ciudad Trujillo

people.name: Tukuitiro Oroui
people.role: Member of Japanese commercial delegation (spelling noted as doubtful in original text; possibly Takutaro Oroui)

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the Dominican government's expulsion of a five-man Japanese commercial delegation suspected of espionage through excessive photography.
subfiles.from: Eugene M. Hinkle, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, U.S. Legation, Ciudad Trujillo
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 615: Hinkle reports Dominican authorities gave a five-man Japanese 'commercial delegation'—including a former Japanese legation secretary from Mexico City—ten days to leave on espionage suspicion over excessive photography and no real business; they departed for Havana by SS Cuba on Feb 3, 1939.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 615: Expulsion of Japanese Commercial Mission from Dominican Republic
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D. C.
